scope: Leadership product-discovery report with expanded search/autocomplete experiments.

methodology.collection_method: Rendered search pages plus browser-context Shopify suggest API responses.
methodology.scoring_note: Scores are bounded public-evidence relevance judgments from result counts, sampled product titles, and suggestion payloads. They are not analytics, conversion, or revenue measurements.

prior_ecommerce_evidence_used.used_for: Existing browse, cart, mobile, policy, camp autocomplete, and local-assessment reference context.

opportunity_model.basis: Directional model from public experiments only. Dollar impact requires site-search usage, conversion rate, AOV, revenue, and analytics segmentation.
opportunity_model.rationale: Search and browse already recover many intents. The main upside is earlier assistance and consistency: fewer shoppers should have to press enter, reformulate, or know exact English catalog language.

competitor_evidence.purpose: Clarify the earlier competitor limitation and add a bounded opportunity story around national outdoor retailers and organic versus sponsored/retail-media visibility.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether the site understands common typing variations such as missing apostrophes, plurals, shorthand, and gender wording.
concepts.why_it_matters: Good normalization keeps high-intent shoppers from being punished for normal typing habits.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether the site handles multi-word phrases, slash notation, brand numerals, and product phrases as shopper intent rather than isolated words.
concepts.why_it_matters: Token handling affects whether customers can search naturally instead of memorizing exact product names.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether the site connects customer language to retailer language: shell versus jacket, puffer versus insulated, pack versus backpack, and similar wording.
concepts.why_it_matters: Synonym coverage is often where good search looks expert, because customers rarely use catalog-perfect terminology.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether important fields such as brand, product type, gender, activity, and model name appear to influence what rises first.
concepts.why_it_matters: Strong ranking makes the first few results feel obvious, which is what owners notice when they test their own site.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether broader needs such as trail running, hot-weather hiking, lake day, or gifts expand into useful products.
concepts.why_it_matters: Expansion is where search moves from order-taking to selling: it helps a shopper who knows the use case but not the product name.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether searchable fields include useful product attributes such as UPF, waterproof, quick-dry, merino, polarized, packable, and breathable.
concepts.why_it_matters: Enriched product data lets shoppers search by benefits, materials, and features instead of exact titles.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether Spanish or mixed Spanish-English searches can still guide local and visiting shoppers to the right English-language products.
concepts.why_it_matters: This is a market-access question, not a demographic assumption: bilingual discovery reduces friction when customers search in Spanish, English, or both.
